# What archy does on your machine

archy reads your Python source and, if you ask, edits your AI agents' config
files. This page lists what it touches. **Every claim below is pinned by a test
in [`tests/test_safety_claims.py`](../tests/test_safety_claims.py)**; a sentence
without a test is marked as such. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_safety_claims.py`
to check them against the copy you have.

For vulnerability reporting and scope, see [`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md).

## In one table

| | |
|---|---|
| Network | None. archy's own code imports no networking module, and the test suite makes `connect()` fatal while every read-only command and every MCP tool runs. |
| Subprocesses | `git` only, and only `git -C <project> rev-parse` and `git -C <project> log`. Both read history; neither changes it. |
| Your analysed code | Parsed with tree-sitter, never imported or executed. |
| Most commands | Write nothing at all (list below). |
| The commands that write | Each writes a fixed, named set of files (table below). |

## Network

- `src/archy` imports none of `socket`, `ssl`, `http`, `urllib`, `requests`,
  `httpx`, `aiohttp`, `ftplib`, `smtplib`, `poplib`, `imaplib`, `telnetlib`,
  `xmlrpc`, `websockets`, `websocket`.
  (`test_source_imports_no_network_module`)
- A second test catches what an import scan cannot (a call built with
  `__import__`, or a dependency): with `socket.connect`, `connect_ex`,
  `sendto`, `getaddrinfo` and `create_connection` all made to fail, the
  read-only commands and all 14 MCP tools still run, and nothing attempts a
  connection. (`test_runtime_attempts_no_connection`)
- The MCP server (`archy mcp`) serves over stdio. It opens no listener.

Installing archy is a different matter: `pip`, `uv` or `uvx` download it from
PyPI. That is your package manager, not archy.

## Subprocesses

Only these modules run a subprocess: `coupling.py`, `gitlog.py`, `hotspots.py`
and `history.py`. None uses a shell, `os.system`, `os.popen` or `Popen`.
(`test_only_git_modules_use_subprocess`)

Running the command matrix records every subprocess call: each is
`git -C <project> rev-parse ...` or `git -C <project> log ...`, and both
subcommands are actually exercised.
(`test_runtime_subprocesses_are_read_only_git`)

`archy contracts` and `archy check --contracts` run import-linter inside the
same Python process, not as a subprocess.

## Your analysed code is not run

archy parses source text. A module whose top level writes a file is parsed,
appears in the graph, and its side effect never happens, across the read-only
commands and all MCP tools. (`test_analysed_code_is_never_executed`)

## Commands that write nothing

These leave every file in the project and in your home directory unchanged, and
each exits 0 (a usage error would "write nothing" for free):

`check`, `cycles`, `score`, `graph`, `dsm`, `hotspots`, `coupling`,
`duplicates`, `conventions`, `brief`, `what-to-refactor-next`, `trend`, `diff`,
`render` (it prints HTML to stdout unless you pass `--out`), `impact`,
`affected`. (`test_read_only_command_writes_nothing`)

`install --print-config <agent>` also writes nothing.
(`test_install_print_config_writes_nothing`)

## Commands that write

| Command | What it writes | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `archy snapshot` | `.archy/baseline.json` in the project | `test_snapshot_writes_only_the_baseline` |
| `archy score --record` | appends to `.archy/history.jsonl` | `test_score_record_writes_only_the_history_file` |
| `archy index sync` | `.archy/index.db`, a parse cache; `archy index clear` deletes it | `test_index_sync_writes_only_the_cache` |
| `archy render --out FILE` | `FILE` only | `test_render_out_writes_only_the_named_file` |
| `archy install --target all` (global, the default) | the 11 files listed below, in your home directory | `test_global_install_writes_exactly_the_listed_files_in_home` |
| `archy install --target all --location local` | the 10 files listed below, in the project | `test_local_install_writes_exactly_the_listed_files_in_the_project` |
| `archy uninstall` | removes archy's entries from those files | `test_uninstall_removes_what_install_added` |
| `archy mcp` | see next section | `test_mcp_tools_write_only_cache_and_baseline` |

Install, global (paths relative to your home directory):

```
.claude.json                       .codex/AGENTS.md
.claude/CLAUDE.md                  .codex/config.toml
.claude/settings.json              .config/opencode/AGENTS.md
.cursor/mcp.json                   .config/opencode/opencode.json
.cursor/rules/archy.mdc            .continue/mcpServers/archy.yaml
                                   .continue/rules/archy.md
```

Install, local (paths relative to the project):

```
.mcp.json   CLAUDE.md   .claude/settings.json   AGENTS.md   opencode.json
.codex/config.toml   .cursor/mcp.json   .cursor/rules/archy.mdc
.continue/mcpServers/archy.yaml   .continue/rules/archy.md
```

These lists are what a **clean** home directory or project gets. On an existing
setup, install edits those files in place. By default `archy install` only
configures the agents it detects; `--target all` is what the test uses. The
Windows locations (`%APPDATA%`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`) are not covered by a test.

## The MCP server

Every MCP tool except `archy_snapshot` is annotated read-only. While serving,
they write at most one thing, `.archy/index.db`, the same derived cache as above:
the server keeps it warm and refreshes it when your files change.
`archy_snapshot` additionally writes `.archy/baseline.json` and is the only tool
not annotated read-only. No tool writes anywhere else in the project or your home
directory. Deleting `.archy/` is always safe.

## What this page does not claim

- **Writes outside the project and your home directory** (for example the system
  temp directory) are not observed by the tests.
- **`archy conventions --emit-headers --write`** rewrites the derived header
  block inside your source files. It is opt-in and has no test on this page;
  `--check` is the read-only form.
- **`archy simulate`, `archy contracts` and `archy history`** are not in the
  read-only list above, because the test matrix does not run them.
- **Third-party dependencies** (`networkx`, `pydantic`, `click`, `tree-sitter`,
  `mcp`, `watchdog`, and `import-linter` with the `contracts` extra) run
  inside archy's process. The runtime test shows none opens a connection on the
  paths it exercises; it does not audit their code.
- **Release checksums.** PyPI publishes a SHA-256 for the wheel and the sdist on
  each file's page. archy publishes no separate checksum file.

Done. I saved it to memory as a standing rule, and I applied it to #692 right away. From now on, every adversarial review of archy work will include archy's own tools: `check`, `cycles --strict`, `contracts`, `affected`/`impact` on the changed files, `diff`, and `hotspots` when source changes. Their output goes into the reviewer's brief and into the findings.

Here is what archy says about #692:

- **`archy check`:** no violations, 47 of 48 modules covered.
- **`archy cycles --strict`:** no cycles.
- **`archy contracts`:** 26 kept, 0 broken.
- **`archy affected`:** the only changed Python module is `tests.test_safety_claims`. Nothing imports it and no tests are affected, so the PR has no structural blast radius. The new test module is one added graph node.
- **Score:** unchanged in character, with acyclicity at 1.000, since no `src/` file moved.

The limit of this evidence: archy confirms the PR doesn't disturb the architecture, but it can't tell whether a test is blind. That is what the mutation runs are for.

The adversarial reviewer launched before this rule, so its brief doesn't include the archy commands. I'll fold the output above into the final report rather than rerun it. I'm waiting on its findings before committing the DRY and README fixes.

## 1. Over-claims (page vs test)

**HIGH. "every MCP tool is called" is false for `archy_module_view`.**
- The page says "every MCP tool is called". My probe of `_call_every_mcp_tool` (same args) printed `archy_module_view True ERR ToolError ... 1 validation error for archy_module_viewArguments`. The required `module` argument is never supplied, so pydantic rejects the call before the tool body runs.

- Mutation `6b`: `archy_module_view` writes `Path.home()/".leak"`. Result: **30 passed (survived, real blind spot)**. The same hole exists in `test_mcp_tools_write_only_cache_and_baseline`, which suppresses the exception for that tool. The page's "No tool writes anywhere else ... your home directory" is unpinned for that tool.
- Other tools "answer", but I did not check that they reach their write-capable branches.

**HIGH. "`archy mcp` serves over stdio and opens no listener" has no test, although the page says every claim has one.**
- No test invokes `mcp` or inspects its transport.
- `9b`: `create_server().run(transport="sse")` in the `mcp` command. **30 passed (survived).**
- `9`: binding a TCP listener in `mcp` was only caught because `import socket` trips the static import scan, not because of the stdio claim.
- `3c`: `importlib.import_module("soc"+"ket").socket().bind(...).listen()` in a read-only command. **30 passed (survived).** The runtime test patches only connect-side calls, never `bind`, `listen` or `accept`.

**MEDIUM. "Network: None" and "the test makes connect() fatal" are weaker than they read.** The patch covers `connect`, `connect_ex`, `sendto`, `getaddrinfo` and `create_connection`.
- `3b` (`getattr(importlib.import_module("soc"+"ket"), "gethostbyname")("example.com")`) survived. A DNS lookup is not intercepted.
- `3d` (`importlib.import_module("_soc"+"ket").socket().connect(("127.0.0.1", 9))`) survived. The raw `_socket` class is not patched.
- Caught: `3a` (`importlib.import_module("urllib.request").urlopen`) and `3e` (`asyncio.open_connection`).

**MEDIUM. "None uses a shell, `os.system`, `os.popen` or `Popen`" and "only these modules run a subprocess" rest on a syntactic scan.** All of these survived in `cli.py`:
- `4a` `os.spawnvp(os.P_WAIT, "true", ["true"])`.
- `4b` `asyncio.run(asyncio.create_subprocess_exec("true"))`.
- `4d` `import os as o; o.system("true")`.
- `4e` `from os import system; system("true")`.
- Only `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.exec*` and `subprocess.Popen` are named, and only when written with the bare `os`/`subprocess` names. `spawn*`, `posix_spawn`, aliases and `from`-imports pass.
- `subprocess.run` is the only recorded call. `subprocess.check_output` was caught only because it calls `run` internally (`4c`).
- `4f` (a new `subprocess.run(["true"])` in `cli.py`) was caught, by 2 tests.

**MEDIUM. The git claim ("`git -C <project> rev-parse` and `log`, both read history, neither changes it") checks only argv[0], argv[1] and argv[3].**
- Caught: `5a` (a `push` run through `subprocess.run`), `5b` (`config` via `history._git`), and `5e` (`-C /`, incidentally, with 5 failures).
- `5c`: adding `--output=.git/leak` to the `git log` in `hotspots.py`. **Survived.** I confirmed outside the harness that git really writes `.git/leak` for `git log --output=...`. A flag after the subcommand that makes `log` write a file is not checked.

**LOW. "leave every file in the project ... unchanged" does not cover `.git`.**
- `_snapshot` excludes `.git`, and anything outside the project and home is unobserved.
- `2b` (a read-only command writes `proj/.git/leak`) **survived**. `6c` (an MCP tool writes `.git/leak`) **survived**. `2c` (writes `/tmp/archy_leak_outside`) survived.
- The page admits the temp-dir gap. It does not mention `.git`, which is inside the project.
- Controls: `1` (read-only command writes to HOME) and `2` (writes `proj/leak.txt`) were both caught. `6a` (an MCP tool writes `.archy/other.json`) was caught.

**LOW. The install and uninstall claims are narrower than the page's wording.**
- `7a` (cursor adapter writes an extra `.cursor/extra.json`) was caught. `7c` (a `.bak` copy of a pre-existing file) was caught, incidentally.
- `7b`: cursor `mcp.json` uninstall changed to `unrender=delete_file`, so uninstall deletes a shared file outright. **30 passed (survived).** The page says uninstall "removes archy's entries from those files". The test only asserts that no file still contains "archy", and a deleted file satisfies that.
- `7d`: `run_uninstall` writes `~/leak`. **30 passed (survived).** The uninstall test never diffs the project, and it does not diff home beyond the `"archy" not in text` loop over the listed files.
- `7e` (writing in `runner.print_config`) is **inert**. The CLI uses `preview_config`, so the mutation was never reached. I did not mutate `preview_config`.
- Install on an existing config is untested, as the page says. The edit-in-place claim ("edits those files in place") is therefore unpinned.

**Annotation claim:** the flips `8a` (`archy_check` not read-only) and `8b` (`archy_snapshot` read-only) were both caught. That part is sound.

## 2. Fixture drift

- `_call_every_mcp_tool` swallows every exception. One tool of 14 never runs (`archy_module_view`, above), and the `>= 12` floor guarantees nothing about which tools ran.
- The 16-command matrix and the git exercise look real. All 16 exit 0, and the recorded git subcommands must be exactly `{rev-parse, log}`. I did not find a usage no-op there. I did not check whether `trend` and `diff` do real work beyond exiting 0.
- Tool count: `INSTALL.md` says 14 tools. The test asserts `>= 14`, so an added tool is never exercised by name.

## 3. Contradictions with `docs/INSTALL.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `README.md`

- **`docs/INSTALL.md`, MEDIUM.** The installed MCP registration is `uvx archy mcp`, which "is fetched and run on demand from PyPI". The SAFETY table says "Network: None", with only a one-line caveat about the package manager. A reader will not learn from SAFETY that the registration the installer writes triggers a PyPI fetch on client launch.
- **`SECURITY.md`:** its threat model says install "perform[s] no other side effects". That is the same untested uninstall surface as `7b` and `7d`.
- **README link:** the heading change `## Reporting security issues` to `### Reporting security issues` is fine, and the new link is consistent with `SECURITY.md`.
- **Count:** the page lists 16 read-only commands, matching `READ_ONLY_COMMANDS`. The page says 11 global and 10 local install files, matching the constants.

## Note on the working tree

`tests/test_safety_claims.py` and `README.md` are modified in the real tree (the `_mcp_args` helper refactor). I tested HEAD, so the refactor is not covered. It does not change any of the above.</result>

Every other MCP test in this suite calls the `_run_*` helpers directly, which
proves the payloads are right but never starts a server or speaks the protocol.
That gap is why `archy.mcp_compat` needs this file: aliasing `FastMCP` to
`MCPServer` makes both majors *import*, and signature comparison shows they take
the same arguments, but neither fact proves they put the same bytes on the wire.

archy's documented contract is a claim about SDK behavior, not call shape:

- every tool advertises an `outputSchema` derived from its return type
- results carry `structuredContent` alongside the text block
- read-only annotations survive to `tools/list`

So this drives an actual client over stdio: initialize, list, call. It passes on
whichever major is installed, which is what makes it the check that catches a
2.x divergence the alias cannot -- run it under both to clear a ceiling bump.

Kept out of `test_mcp.py` deliberately: these spawn a subprocess and take
seconds rather than milliseconds, and they fail for a different reason (the
transport, not the payload).
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import archy
from archy.affected import DELETED_OR_RENAMED_REASON

    (app / "core" / "model_registry.py").write_text("REGISTRY = {}\n")
    (app / "commands" / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (app / "commands" / "setup_user.py").write_text("x = 1\n")
    (root / "archy.yaml").write_text(

content.text:
I fixed the two most critical review findings in PR #692, filed the other six as tickets, and pushed the fixes. The full suite passes (1713 tests), and `archy check`, `cycles --strict` and `contracts` are clean on the branch.

**Fixed in the PR**
1. **`archy_module_view` was never actually called.** Its required `module` argument was missing and the error was swallowed. A write to your home directory from that tool slipped through, so I confirmed that mutation is now red. The helpers no longer swallow errors, and the test now fails if any tool refuses.
2. **The "stdio, no listener" claim had no test.** A new test runs the real `archy mcp` command, checks that it answers on stdout, and uses `lsof` to confirm it opens no listening socket. Switching the command to `sse` now turns it red.

Along the way I hit one bug of my own. The new test used `select.select`, which failed once earlier tests had left file descriptors open above 1023. It only failed in the full suite, so I caught it there and switched to `selectors`.

**Filed as tickets**

| # | Issue | Label |
|---|---|---|
| #693 | Network check misses DNS lookups, raw `_socket`, and bind/listen | good second issue |
| #694 | Subprocess scan bypassed by `os.spawn*`, asyncio subprocesses, aliased imports | good second issue |
| #695 | Git argument check ignores flags after the subcommand (`log --output=...`) | good first issue |
| #696 | `.git` is left out of the file-tree snapshot | good first issue |
| #697 | Uninstall is weakly tested and nothing covers an existing config | good second issue |
| #698 | Docs: the installed `uvx archy mcp` entry fetches from PyPI | good first issue |

I called a ticket "second" when it needs design or reading the installer internals, and "first" when it's a small, well-specified change to one test or doc. `docs/SAFETY.md` now lists all six as known gaps, so the page doesn't claim more than the tests prove.

I also removed two pre-existing em dashes from the README and merged a duplicated MCP-arguments block. Both were DeepWork findings.

The PR is ready for you to merge. I didn't offer another review round, since this one just ran, but say so if you want one on the new commit.
